h: Queens, tombs and a famous song
p: Framlingham's history didn't stop with the Bigods. In 1553 Mary Tudor rallied her supporters at the castle before being proclaimed queen, so this quiet Suffolk town played its part in one of England's big Tudor dramas. Have that in mind as you look out from the walls, because the view is the same one her supporters would have seen.

Allow two to three hours for the castle, then save time for St Michael's Church, a short stroll away in the town. Inside are the magnificent tombs of the Howard family, including Thomas Howard, 3rd Duke of Norfolk, and Henry Fitzroy, the illegitimate son of Henry VIII. Their carved monuments are some of the finest of their kind, and they make a brilliant follow-on from the castle story.

Behind the castle, the mere is a peaceful spot for a walk and a bit of birdwatching, with lovely views back up to the walls. It's a nice way to see the castle from a different angle, so take the kids round before you head into town.

Music fans will probably know that Ed Sheeran grew up here, and his song Castle on the Hill is about this very place. The town centre around Market Hill has independent shops, cafés and pubs for refuelling. If you've a car and a full day, Suffolk's coast is close, with Orford's castle and quayside, Aldeburgh's beach and Snape Maltings all within a comfortable drive.
